# ISSUE-380 implementation plan

Expose one coordinator-owned description of existing sandbox tools through doctor, task inspection, and role bundles. Keep execution permissions and scheduling unchanged. This is a sensitive discovery change, with a bounded investigation before integration; implementation requires the configured independent human plan gate.

## Dimensions and budget

Approved dimensions: multi_area / unknown / sensitive; execution profile: investigation. Estimate 10–14 hours for investigation, implementation, focused verification and review within the 16-hour claim budget. Reopen scope if the probe reveals a need for a new permission mechanism or transport.

## What we know

- Task preflight loads configuration from authoritative state.BaseSHA before selecting agents (`internal/workflow/engine.go:324`, especially the LoadConfigAt call). Doctor instead inspects repository configuration (`internal/cli/doctor.go:26`). Their policy contexts must be explicit, never presented as equivalent task authorization.
- `PreflightResult` currently exposes execution, blockers and browser prose, with no shared tool report (`internal/workflow/engine.go:157`). Dry-run always writes JSON despite a separate --json flag (`internal/cli/work.go:154`, `:255`).
- Tool definitions and enforced argument limits exist in `executorTools` and `ToolExecutor.Call` (`internal/sandbox/tools.go:17`, `:42`): four swarm_* tools, 128 KiB arguments, 1 MiB read/edit files. Executor commands last at most two minutes (`internal/sandbox/executor.go:159`). Native commands have different limits; do not copy executor limits onto them.
- Preflight already checks native/delegated interfaces, role allowlists, authentication and canaries (`internal/agent/configured.go:138`). Inspection reuse is command-local and policy/binary-bound (`internal/sandbox/native.go:238`, `:316`). Launch still checks its boundary.
- Claude uses owned MCP, OpenCode 2 has owned MCP permission mappings, and OhMyPi uses RPC host tools (`internal/sandbox/delegated.go:186`, `:208`, `:277`; `internal/sandbox/omp.go:22`). Native Codex only receives the owned MCP browser connection for eligible Linux developer/tester roles (`internal/sandbox/codex_browser.go:14`).
- Bundle compilation uses approved-base content and safefs (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:789`, `:910`). Both PR bundles and interactive claims call it (`internal/workspace/pr.go:22`; `internal/cli/claim.go:123`).
- Scheduling is string matching of node declarations, including existing nil-profile behavior (`internal/node/profile.go:91`; `internal/cli/selection.go:161`). It is not proof of sandbox execution availability.
- Browser support is already present in this snapshot, including CheckBrowserProfile and documentation. Preserve it; do not repeat #370 setup work.

## What we are assuming

- An additive report in existing packages can cover this without a new contract field. Verify with the bounded probe below.
- Existing dependency preparation results can supply safe readiness information without extra fetching. Verify against Dependencies and preflight ordering; distinguish not prepared/not probed from unavailable.
- This exported snapshot corresponds to the approved base. Git status failed because there is no .git metadata; approved-base comparison is unavailable here. No new production source file is prescribed. Before creating the required changelog fragment, the developer must choose a path absent at the approved base using git cat-file in the real worktree. Never overwrite an existing fragment.

## Open questions and bounded investigation

Spend at most 90 minutes in implementation on a reversible, injected-probe prototype in existing sandbox/agent test files. Exercise native Codex plus all four delegated mappings, developer and read-only roles, browser disabled/enabled, denied policy and canary failure. Feed identical typed results into a text formatter and JSON encoder; prove host paths and seeded secrets cannot escape. No authenticated model invocation, dependency downloads, new grants or host fallback.

Record the matrix, commands, observations, unresolved cases and proceed/revise decision in `.swarm/active/CAPABILITY_DECISION.md` (absent in the supplied active directory). The decision artifact is evidence, never an authorization input. Proceed with the design below if reporting can reuse current authorization and probes. Otherwise reopen the plan at the human gate with the smallest identified gap; do not create scheduling names or new permissions.

Live harness execution, real systemd/cgroup/browser qualification and approved-base comparison cannot be established from this restricted snapshot. Put those checks in the PR review checklist; they do not block implementing deterministic coverage.

## Model and architectural decision

Keep typed report definitions and fixed reason/action vocabulary in existing `internal/sandbox/tools.go`; assemble selected harness/role reports in `internal/agent/configured.go` using existing runner resolution and sandbox inspections. Workspace consumes immutable coordinator-supplied report data and renders it; it must not import agent or execute probes while compiling Markdown.

Each entry includes stable identifier, actual harness-visible tool/command and transport, supported operations, execution boundary, role and read-only restrictions, typed limits, logical artifact locations, declared/requested status, authorized status, runtime status (available/unavailable/not_probed), and a fixed reason code with fixed actionable text. Overall usable is the conjunction of authorization and successful applicable runtime verification. Not-probed never means available. Use a deterministic ordering and schema version. Report successful probe categories without captured output. Suggested finite reasons: policy_denied, role_denied, unsupported_boundary, missing_dependency, interface_unqualified, canary_failed, not_prepared, not_probed; map internal failures without formatting arbitrary error strings.

Describe workspace/scratch/artifact paths in sandbox-relative terms. Never include host cache paths, environment values, tokens, identities, executable absolute paths or raw stdout/stderr in the capability report. List shell/file transport separately from browser readiness and dependency/toolchain preparation. Coordinator prefetch is preparation, not an agent network tool. Report only resolved ecosystem/toolchain facts; do not claim a binary exists inside the boundary solely because host LookPath succeeds.

Mandatory means required by existing selected execution/role policy or explicitly enabled approved browser profile. Preserve those existing preflight failures before claiming. Optional unrequested browser support is labeled unavailable/not enabled without becoming a blocker. WorkUnit required_capabilities remains node selection metadata: expose that distinction and preserve MatchesCapabilities behavior exactly. No new tool identifiers are inserted into scheduling lists.

## Exact touchpoints and implementation sequence

1. Complete the bounded probe and decision artifact. Audit limits and actual operation mappings in tools.go, executor.go, native.go, delegated.go, omp.go and codex_browser.go; preserve launch settings unchanged.
2. Modify `internal/sandbox/tools.go` for report types/formatting and reuse concrete limits instead of duplicating magic numbers. Modify `internal/agent/configured.go` to provide structured inspection alongside the existing PreflightWithOptions compatibility entry point. Reuse native InspectionSession and existing CheckToolExecutor/CheckBrowserProfile; propagate context cancellation and bounded deadlines. Failed canaries remain hard failures. Never run candidate commands to discover grants.
3. Modify `internal/workflow/engine.go` PreflightResult/preflight to carry per-role reports from approved configuration plus resolved dependency preparation. Inspect-only returns blockers without taking a lease; execution refuses mandatory failures before lease acquisition. Recheck runtime prerequisites at launch and refresh role descriptions rather than reuse stale availability from a prior command.
4. Modify `internal/cli/doctor.go` to render the shared report in human and --json output with an explicit repository-inspection policy context. Modify `internal/cli/work.go` to retain existing default dry-run JSON and add a real --format=json|text selector for dry-run, default json; --json remains a structured-output request and conflicts with --format=text. Do not change ordinary work output. Both formats use identical fields/reasons; same-context fixtures must agree across doctor and dry-run. Task inspection remains authoritative only when based on its approved SHA.
5. Modify `internal/workspace/worktree.go` CompileHarnessBundleAt/compileHarnessBundle, `internal/workspace/pr.go` CompilePRHarnessBundleAt, `internal/workflow/engine.go` compileExecutionBundle and `internal/cli/claim.go` to pass coordinator-owned role reports through an additive typed option. Update affected callers identified by compile errors/search. Write the report into SYSTEM_PROMPT.md using existing safefs managed writes. If no runtime report is supplied, say not probed rather than infer availability. Never read a candidate-written report as authority. Regenerate at role launch; imported Markdown cannot change executor permissions. Align existing delegated/native browser prompt prefixes in `internal/sandbox/delegated.go` and `internal/sandbox/codex_browser.go` with the same formatter so they cannot promise extra operations. Read-only roles must clearly distinguish exposed tool names from writable operations denied by the boundary.
6. Extend existing tests in tools/executor/native/delegated test coverage, agent adapters/isolation/browser tests, workflow dependencies/inspection tests, workspace bundle tests, and CLI doctor/execution tests. Add regressions that fail on old behavior for candidate grants and secret-bearing probe failures. Do not weaken boundary tests.
7. Update `docs/harness/README.md`, all four `docs/harness/{codex,claude,opencode,omp}.md` guides and `docs/developer.md` with policy context, report interpretation, existing real commands and the newly implemented dry-run format selector. Add one absent-at-base fragment under changes/unreleased using that directory's established format. Add a PR checklist for live harness/OS checks. No CI, scheduler or task contract changes.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved inputs or gates.

- Entry points: sandbox/tools.go:17 (definitions), agent/configured.go:138 (preflight), workflow/engine.go:157 and :324 (report/preclaim), cli/doctor.go:25 (outputs), cli/work.go:154 (dry-run), workspace/worktree.go:789 and :910 (bundle), workspace/pr.go:22 and cli/claim.go:123 (other bundle paths). Paths above are relative to internal/ unless already qualified.
- Extend fixtures/tests: TestDryRunReportsIsolationBlockersWithoutClaim; TestBrowserProfileDoctor; TestBrowserProfileConfiguredPropagation; TestInspectionCommandSessionReusesPreclaimInspection; TestInspectionPreflightFailureStopsBeforeClaim; TestBrowserProfilePreflightNoClaim; workspace bundle_guidance_test.go; sandbox ToolExecutorBoundary and NativeCodexBoundary tests. Keep authenticated integration fixtures opt-in.
- Exact focused commands are D1–D4 in TEST_PLAN.md. Record results against source identity before handing off; no full-policy rerun by agents.
- Checked assumptions: browser implementation exists (read codex_browser.go/browser.go and guides); dry-run default is JSON (read work.go flag and branch); capabilities are scheduling strings (read node/profile.go and selection.go); no Git metadata is available (git status failed). Runtime availability and all baseline tests remain unverified during planning.
- Reopen if reporting requires enabling a new tool/network permission, redefining required_capabilities, relaxing a canary, importing candidate authority, qualifying OCI, or exceeding the remaining claim budget. Related improvements belong in follow-up WorkUnits.
- What this change breaks: internal/cli/browser_profile_test.go currently expects raw browser failure prose; update assertions to fixed reason/action while retaining fail-closed expectations. execution_test.go and CLI dry-run consumers depend on JSON; preserve default JSON and existing keys, add fields. agent/configured.go callers expect (string,error); preserve wrapper. Bundle callers in workspace/pr.go, cli/claim.go and workflow/engine.go must pass or explicitly omit typed reports; omitted means not probed. Existing delegated.go:186 and codex_browser.go guidance promises tool access; replace duplicate descriptions with accurate shared rendering. Harness guides contain browser/transport explanations; update interpretation while preserving existing invocation/security setup. internal/node/profile_test.go and internal/cli/selection_test.go assert scheduling: preserve unchanged and rerun focused regressions. Search CompileHarnessBundleAt, CompilePRHarnessBundleAt, PreflightWithOptions, browser-profile, effective_plan and swarm_shell again before implementation to catch additional callers and snapshots.

# Criterion 3 test-only repair

Implemented the operator's narrowed repair against the approved plan/test plan and APPROVED review. Changed only `internal/workflow/inspection_session_test.go` and this developer artifact. No production defect was exposed and no production code changed. The existing issue fragment `changes/unreleased/380-tool-capabilities.md` was retained.

## Deterministic coverage

`TestToolCapabilityInjectedBoundaryPreflight` exercises ten cases: failed filesystem, network and read-only canaries, missing Python, and missing Bubblewrap, each as a mandatory boundary failure and as optional diagnostic failure. Each case loads approved isolated policy, obtains the shared per-role report through real workflow preflight, asserts exact fixed reason/action and runtime/usable state, and checks human/JSON reports and blockers exclude seeded raw stderr, secret, username and host path.

Mandatory cases inject a failing result at the existing `sandbox.CheckToolExecutor(ctx)` call. They assert `unavailable` and `Restore the selected runtime prerequisites and rerun inspection.`, then invoke ExecuteWork and verify agent-preflight refusal with no claim. Optional cases inject the same errors through the existing optional browser-entry inspection hook, assert `report_unavailable` and `Rerun inspection; optional report assembly did not complete.`, verify the mandatory transport remains usable, and verify execution-mode preflight succeeds without claiming.

There is no production injection seam for the mandatory probe. The test creates a temporary Go build overlay replacing exactly that single probe invocation, compiles a child test process, and runs the matrix there. A call counter proves the injected probe was reached; replacement-count and nonempty-report assertions prevent vacuous passes. The parent logs all child cases and fails on child failure. The overlay and fixture files are temporary; checked-in production source and runtime enforcement are untouched. Interface inspection still uses the existing qualified fake OpenCode fixture. No boundary or model invocation is needed. This tests handling of failed probe results, not the implementation of the canaries or actual prerequisite discovery.
